chunks: 'In the Book of Ali (peace be upon him) is that every person with a womb relationship is at the status of the womb through which he is connected, except if there happens to be an heir closer to the deceased than him, so he supersedes him.'

key_terms.حَجْب: Hajb — exclusion or barring of an heir; the legal mechanism whereby a closer heir prevents a more distant one from inheriting
key_terms.ذُو الرَّحِمِ: Dhaw al-rahim — those related through womb ties (blood relatives), constituting the third category of heirs after spouses and primary heirs (ashab al-fara'id)
key_terms.كِتَابُ عَلِيٍّ: The Book of Ali — a written collection of rulings and hadith dictated by the Prophet (SAWW) and recorded by Imam Ali (AS); one of the most authoritative sources in Shia jurisprudence
key_terms.مَنْزِلَة: Manzila — station, rank, or status; used here to indicate the legal standing of an heir in the inheritance hierarchy
key_terms.يَجُرُّ بِهِ: Yajurru bihi — 'flows through it' or 'is drawn by it'; metaphor for how inheritance rights are transmitted through the chain of kinship

ai.seo_question: What does the Book of Ali say about womb relations and inheritance in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) cites a ruling from the Book of Ali (AS) — a foundational jurisprudential text attributed to Imam Ali. The ruling establishes the principle of proximity in inheritance: a relative through blood kinship (dhawi al-arham) holds the inheritance status corresponding to their womb-tie, but is superseded if a closer heir exists. This principle governs the hierarchy of inheritors in Islamic inheritance law, addressing cases where primary heirs (ashab al-fara'id) are absent and secondary heirs (dhawi al-arham) inherit based on their degree of kinship.
